rationale: B wins because its proof discipline is sharper: "Without the pricing model, this angle is an assertion, not a story — get it first" turns a tempting fintech take into a real pitch gate. A has good material, but it lets "When a business-only fintech decides it's ready to be a full-service bank" survive, which overstates both the banking claim and the evidence for a category story. B still needs a haircut on "now wants your paycheck," but it gives the founder fewer fake doors to walk through.
gaps_in_A: "The bank Silicon Valley Bank's collapse built is becoming a mass-market consumer bank" overstates the facts: Mercury lacks a bank charter, and Mercury Personal is initially invite-only, not proven mass-market.

"Mercury will hold consumer deposits without holding a bank charter itself" is legally sloppy. The update says partner banks provide banking services; the cleaner story is who holds the deposits and how that is disclosed.
"well-capitalized, previously B2B-only player" invents a balance-sheet claim. The update gives profitability and 200,000 business customers, not capitalization.

"When a business-only fintech decides it's ready to be a full-service bank" is padded and overbroad. Checking and savings do not make Mercury a full-service bank, and the set admits the trend hook is thin.
gaps_in_B: "now wants your paycheck" invents a payroll/direct-deposit ambition. Consumer checking and savings make that plausible, not proven.
"the SVB-era customer base is being asked to bring their personal money too" assumes existing business customers are the target. The update only says invite-only with a waitlist.

"the market that broke the unprofitable ones" and "customer-acquisition money pit" lean on an outside market thesis. That may be true, but it is not in the supplied update and needs sourcing before it leaves the room.
"the same arrangement that has been the live question in fintech-banking supervision" creates a regulatory-news backdrop without supplied evidence. Good instinct, but it needs a verified peg.
